answer: One defense is bond-weighted admission. A new agent starts at zero standing: it must climb a trellis of small verifiable jobs, each rung escrowing a fresh bond plus a co-signature from a counterparty the operator cannot control. Standing is non-transferable and decays without work, so reputation cannot be rented. A sybil must fund a separate bond, history and counterparty set per identity, so a thousand clones cost a thousand times more yet carry the weight of one. That asymmetry keeps a forged identity from ever heating past a dull ember: copper is posted and slashable, never promised.
